value.title: Reviewer packet — plan 110, Claude Code direct delivery

sections.name: mission
sections.value: Review the composed s110/claude-delivery branch against req-0002. RE-DERIVE THE ACCEPTANCE ARMS BY EXECUTION — do not read my claims and agree with them. Every number in my reports is checkable; check the ones that would change a decision.

value.text: PRIORITY ORDER, from the impl-guide, highest first: (1) is Held ACTUALLY observable on the wire, or still unreachable for a THIRD reason nobody has named; (2) is concurrency REFUSED rather than resolved; (3) is every guard witnessed red before its green; (4) does the honest-receipt vocabulary still refuse to call a timeout Delivered; (5) one row per seat, proven from the launched environment.

RUN THE MUTATIONS YOURSELF. Mine: revert `build_peer_frame(msg, &inbox.origin())` to the literal "uds:pij-daemon" (expect 4 failures); revert classify_status's is_status to the bare type only (expect 5); replace the Held arm in pointer/worker.rs with release_body (expect 2). A mutation report you did not execute is a claim.

THE TEST I TOLD YOU NOT TO TRUST: `the_control_shape_is_what_the_live_cli_actually_emits` stays GREEN under mutation 2. It pins the fixture, it does not guard the decoder. Check whether any OTHER test in this branch has the same shape — reads as a guard, catches nothing. That is the highest-value thing you can find.

CHECK MY EVIDENCE CLASSES. The held and delivered arms are LIVE against real Claude sessions. The refused arm is FAKE-SERVER ONLY — no live refusal was ever observed end to end. If you find me claiming otherwise anywhere, that is a finding. The fixtures in crates/testkit/fixtures/uds/ claim to be RECORDINGS; status-dropped.ndjson is explicitly NOT one.

The gate must be run as `~/.cargo/bin/cargo run -p pij-testkit --bin pij-gate`. A bare cargo here is not the rustup shim and silently runs rustc 1.95.0 against a 1.98.0 pin. If you report a gate result from the wrong compiler, that is a green that lies.
Load BOTH the pij skill and the builder skill. Report findings to pij-fatal-woodpecker via `pij send` — never a modal in your pane.

Adversarial prompt, and I mean it: I am the PM, I authored the evidence base, AND I wrote most of this code. That is a concentration of authorship with no independent check in it — you are the check. Two of my findings today were wrong and were caught by other people (an inverted acceptance criterion caught by the coder; a startup-window finding I had to retract after the prime ruled on it). Assume there is a third.
PM: pij-fatal-woodpecker (author of u-uds and of the PoC the plan is built on).
Coder: pij-familiar-nigel (u-adopt). Its unit is the daemon register path.
Prime: pij-dominant-vicuna reviews after me and before Jordan merges.
